Introduction

About Me

I am Muhammad Kurniawan, a Junior Researcher at the Indonesian Institute for Energy Economics (IIEE) in Jakarta. My work sits at the intersection of power systems engineering and energy economics — building quantitative models that inform Indonesia's energy policy, investment planning, and regional energy security.

I hold a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering (Power System Engineering) from Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember (ITS), Surabaya, graduating in 2025 with a GPA of 3.52/4.00, supported by the Afirmasi Pendidikan Tinggi 3T (ADik) scholarship. My thesis focused on optimal dispatch considering emissions under high renewable energy and energy storage penetration.

My technical work spans power system optimization (AC/DC OPF, unit commitment, economic dispatch), techno-economic feasibility studies, and energy economics & policy analysis. I have contributed to studies for the Java-Madura-Bali, Sulawesi, and North Sulawesi grid systems, with partners including PT PLN, Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA), National Energy Council (DEN), and ViriyaENB.

Long-term, my goal is to contribute to meaningful impact in shaping the future of energy — through research and advisory work grounded in data-driven analysis and evidence-based policy.
